Balanced Diet & Meal Planning

Balanced diet — food groups, meal planning, food pyramid and planning meals for different ages.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Define balanced diet and list food groups
  • Use the food pyramid for meal planning
  • Plan meals for different age groups

In simple words

A balanced diet provides all nutrients in correct amounts and proportions. It includes cereals, pulses, milk, vegetables, fruits, fats and sugars in the right mix.

Meal planning means selecting and combining foods so that each day’s intake meets nutrient needs within the family budget.

Food groups (ICMR)

Food group Examples Main nutrients
Cereals Rice, wheat, ragi, jowar Carbohydrates, energy
Pulses Dal, beans, soya Protein
Milk and products Milk, curd, paneer Calcium, protein
Vegetables Leafy greens, roots Vitamins, minerals, fibre
Fruits Banana, apple, orange Vitamins, minerals
Fats and oils Oil, ghee, nuts Energy, fat-soluble vitamins
Sugar and jaggery Sugar, jaggery Energy

Food pyramid

The food pyramid shows proportions: eat most from the base (cereals, vegetables, fruits), less from the middle (milk, pulses, meat), and least from the top (fats, oils, sugar).

Meal planning points

  • Include all food groups every day.
  • Use seasonal and local foods — cheaper and fresher.
  • Consider age, activity, health and budget.
  • Pregnant women, children and sick people need special planning.

🔴 Balanced diet definition

A balanced diet provides all nutrients in correct amounts and proportions, using a variety of foods from all food groups.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Diet counselling — explain balanced diet using the food pyramid; keep it simple and practical.
  • Hospital diets — ensure the patient’s meal includes all food groups as prescribed.
  • Budget planning — suggest low-cost nutrient-rich foods (seasonal vegetables, local pulses, eggs).
  • Special needs — plan for pregnancy, lactation, infancy, old age and illness.
  • Patient teaching — teach the “plate method”: half vegetables/fruits, quarter cereals, quarter protein.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. A balanced diet provides all nutrients in correct amounts and proportions.
  2. Food groups: cereals, pulses, milk, vegetables, fruits, fats, sugar.
  3. Food pyramid: eat most cereals/vegetables/fruits; least fats/oils/sugar.
  4. Meal planning considers age, activity, health and budget.
  5. Plate method: half vegetables/fruits, quarter cereals, quarter protein.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Seasonal and local foods are cheaper and fresher.
  2. Pregnant women, children and sick people need special meal planning.
  3. Combine cereals with pulses for better protein quality.
  4. Limit sugar, oil and junk food.

📌 Memory trick

Plate method: “Half veg/fruit, quarter cereal, quarter protein.”

60-second revision

  • Balanced diet = all nutrients in correct amounts/proportions.
  • Food groups: cereals, pulses, milk, vegetables, fruits, fats, sugar.
  • Pyramid: base = eat most; top = eat least.
  • Plate: half veg/fruit, quarter cereal, quarter protein.
  • Plan for age, activity, health, budget.

Test yourself

A balanced diet provides:

Answer: B. A balanced diet provides all nutrients in correct amounts and proportions.

At the base of the food pyramid are:

Answer: B. Cereals, vegetables and fruits form the base — eat most.

Which is the cheapest way to improve protein quality?

Answer: B. Combining cereals (rice/wheat) with pulses (dal) improves plant protein quality at low cost.

In the plate method, what fraction is vegetables/fruits?

Answer: B. Half the plate should be vegetables and fruits.

Meal planning considers:

Answer: B. Meal planning considers age, activity, health status and budget.
